episode.tagline: Most of what we think of as quintessentially Indian originated elsewhere. So what? Culture is a khichdi -- and that's delightful!
episode.about: In this episode, Amit and Ajay talk about the amazing khichdi called culture -- and how food, clothes, language, architecture all evolve in a giant melting pot of influences. Just as salmon sushi is not from Japan, most Indian food is not from India, and that's fine. It doesn't matter where influences come from -- once they get here, they're ours!

items.content: Amit sneaks in proof that English is Indian: the word juggernaut comes from Jagannath, 'and indeed the show, one could argue, is like a…
Amit imagines Norway's salmon glut spilling into the streets: classrooms so full of salmon that kids couldn't go to school, police…
Ajay tells half-Bengali Amit that some say the rasgulla's geographical indicator belongs to Odisha and that the idea was brought by the…
Ajay's punchline to Frederick the Great's guarded potato gardens: 'This is the best way to make something work. It is to announce that…
Amit on bananas: 'in the best way possible, we are a banana republic.' The bananas we gave the world went, 'in the worst way possible',…
Amit savours the 'Pushpesh Pant pet peeves': the tyranny of the tandoor, the curse of the curry and the myth of Mughlai. 'And if he wore…
Ajay swears off basmati rice, calling it a tyranny. Amit, alliterating in Pushpesh Pant's honour, upgrades it to 'the barbarism of…
How to measure someone's distance from a Maharashtrian village: say 'wangi' and you're close; 'baingan' is one step removed; then…
As Ajay explains Kutchi pride, Amit butts in: 'If Kutchis invented the underwear, the kachha, which is so impressive to me, but carry on.'
Bombay restaurants all serving paneer butter masala reminds Amit of Pratap Bhanu Mehta, 'because he's called PBM'.
Ajay: 'I'm no friend of rap music, but surely there should be a Rabindra rap sangeet.' Amit admits that as a kid he thought rap was…
Amit's definition of culture, which he says they should rename the show after: 'Everything is everything.'
Amit's sign-off after Ajay's sourdough and kefir sermon: 'May you have peace in your life, but ferment in your food.'
George Bernard Shaw's Caesar and Cleopatra, quoted by Ajay: 'He is a barbarian who thinks that the customs of his tribe and island are…
Ajay uses the quip 'a language is a dialect with a navy' to argue that pre-Independence Hindustani was really many dialects, flattened…
Ajay notes that radio was first abused on a large scale by Mussolini, the start of mass media's homogenising era.
Monsoon Wedding: Amit recalls a character constantly eating marigolds, the 'Indian' wedding flower that actually came from Mexico.
The Japanese monkeys who learned to wash sandy rice in seawater, cited by Ajay as documented proof that non-human animals have culture.
The galouti kebab legend: a nawab with bad teeth needed meat that melted in the mouth, and a classic dish was born.
